title: pMarineViewer Action Buttons
prompt: How are pMarineViewer action buttons configured to post variables such as `DEPLOY`, `MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE`, and `RETURN`, and what mistakes make a button appear but not affect the mission?

notebook.text:
Action buttons in pMarineViewer are configured in the .moos mission file within the pMarineViewer configuration block
1
. These buttons allow users to "poke" the MOOSDB with specific variable-value pairs to control the mission
2
3
.
Configuring Action Buttons
You can configure up to twenty buttons (using parameters button_one through button_twenty)
1
4
. The configuration uses a specific syntax where the right-hand side is a '#'-separated list containing the button label and one or more variable-value pairs
5
.
Configuration Syntax Example:
// Illustrative configuration snippet
ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer
{
  // Button 1: Deploy the vehicle and put it in 'drive'
  button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false
  
  // Button 2: Command the vehicle to return
  button_two = RETURN # RETURN=true
}

Labels: Any component in the list that does not contain an '=' is interpreted as the button’s label
5
.
Multiple Pokes: A single button click can trigger multiple variable pokes (e.g., setting both DEPLOY=true and MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false simultaneously)
3
.
Variable Types: pMarineViewer uses a heuristic to determine the data type: if the value is non-numerical (like true), it is posted as a string; if it is numerical, it is posted as a double
5
. To force a numerical value to be a string, you must surround it with quotes
5
.
Common Mistakes (Why a button appears but has no effect)
If a button is visible on the GUI but clicking it does not affect the vehicle's mission, the following issues are the most likely causes, ranked from most common to least common:
Missing Bridges (Shoreside-Vehicle Topology): In most multi-vehicle missions, pMarineViewer runs on a "shoreside" community
6
7
. When you click a button, the poke happens only in the shoreside MOOSDB
8
. If you have not configured uFldShoreBroker (or pShare) to bridge that variable to the vehicle's community, the vehicle will never receive the command
8
.
Case Sensitivity: MOOS variables and their string values are case-sensitive
11
12
. If a behavior condition is looking for DEPLOY=true but your button posts deploy=true or DEPLOY=TRUE, the condition will not be met
13
14
.
Spelling Mismatches: A common pitfall is the legacy misspelling of "override" in MOOS. The helm traditionally uses MOOS_MANUAL_OVERIDE (one 'r')
15
16
. While the helm has been updated to respect the correct spelling (MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE) as well, other applications might only listen for one specific version
15
16
.
Heuristic Type Mismatch: If a behavior expects a string (e.g., DEPLOY="true") but pMarineViewer posts a double, or vice-versa, the receiving application may ignore the post
17
18
.
Behavior Logic and Initializations:
The button only pokes the variable; a behavior in the .bhv file must actually have a condition listening for that variable (e.g., condition = DEPLOY=true) to take action
14
19
.
If the helm is in a MALCONFIG state due to a behavior error, it will not process mission control pokes
20
21
.
Helm State (Manual Override): If you poke DEPLOY=true but the vehicle is still in PARK because MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE is still true, the vehicle will not move
22
23
. The DEPLOY button must typically set the override variable to false to transition the helm into the DRIVE state
23
24
.

chatgpt.text:
In pMarineViewer, action buttons are configured inside the ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer block of the .moos mission file. They post MOOS variables when clicked, usually to trigger helm autonomy or mode changes.

A normal pattern looks like this:

ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer
{
  AppTick   = 4
  CommsTick = 4

  // Button name shown in viewer, then one or more MOOS posts
  action = DEPLOY=true # DEPLOY=true
  action = MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false
  action = RETURN=true # RETURN=true

  // Often combined into one useful button
  action = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false
  action = RETURN # RETURN=true
}

The important pattern is:

action = BUTTON_LABEL # VAR=value # VAR2=value

So this:

action = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false

creates a button labeled DEPLOY. When clicked, it posts:

DEPLOY = true
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE = false

That is useful because the helm often needs both:

DEPLOY == true
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE == false

before autonomous behaviors are allowed to run.

Common mission variables:

DEPLOY = true

Usually enables mission behaviors whose .bhv conditions include:

condition = DEPLOY == true
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE = false

Usually releases manual override so pHelmIvP can take control.

RETURN = true

Often activates return-to-home or station-return behavior if a behavior is conditioned on it, for example:

condition = RETURN == true

A typical button set might be:

ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer
{
  AppTick   = 4
  CommsTick = 4

  action = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false
  action = RETURN # RETURN=true
  action = STATION_KEEP # DEPLOY=false # RETURN=false
  action = STOP # DEPLOY=false # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=true
}

The button can appear in pMarineViewer but still not affect the mission for several reasons.

First, the button may be posting the wrong variable name. MOOS variable names are exact. If the behavior condition says:

condition = DEPLOY == true

but the button posts:

Deploy = true

or:

DEPLOY_ALL = true

then the behavior will never see the intended variable.

Second, the button may post the wrong value type or spelling. If the behavior checks:

condition = RETURN == true

but the button posts:

RETURN=yes

or:

RETURN=1

that may not match the condition you wrote. Use the exact value expected by the .bhv file.

Third, the button may only post DEPLOY=true but forget to clear manual override:

action = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true

If MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE remains true, the helm may stay overridden even though DEPLOY is true. This is one of the most common “button works but vehicle does nothing” failures.

Fourth, the relevant behavior may not actually be conditioned on that variable. For example, posting RETURN=true does nothing unless some behavior or app is watching RETURN.

Fifth, the .bhv file may use a different condition than the button assumes:

condition = RETURN_HOME == true

while the button posts:

RETURN=true

In that case, the viewer button is fine, but the mission logic is not connected to it.

Sixth, the helm may not be running, the behavior file may not have loaded, or the behavior may be idle because of other conditions. For example:

condition = DEPLOY == true
condition = RETURN == false
condition = NAV_X > 0

If any condition is false or missing, the behavior does not run.

Seventh, you may be editing the wrong generated .moos file. In many MOOS-IvP missions, launch scripts generate target .moos files from meta_*.moos templates using nsplug. If you edit the template but do not regenerate, or edit a generated file that gets overwritten at launch, the visible button configuration may not be the one actually running.

To debug it, click the button and watch the variables directly:

Bash
uXMS DEPLOY MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE RETURN

or use:

Bash
uQueryDB DEPLOY
uQueryDB MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE
uQueryDB RETURN

Then check the helm side:

Bash
uHelmScope

You want to confirm three things:

The button posts the variable.

The variable name and value match the .bhv conditions exactly.

pHelmIvP is not blocked by MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE or some other unmet condition.

The clean mental model is: pMarineViewer buttons only post MOOS variables. They do not directly start behaviors. Behaviors start only if the helm sees matching variable conditions in the .bhv file.

Thinking

claude.text:
Great COMP417-adjacent question — this is core MOOS-IvP territory. Let me break it down clearly.

pMarineViewer Action Buttons
How buttons are configured

Buttons are defined in the pMarineViewer block of a .moos mission file. Each button is declared with a numbered parameter like BUTTON_ONE, BUTTON_TWO, etc., using this syntax:

BUTTON_ONE = label=DEPLOY # var=DEPLOY # sval=true \
           : var=MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE # sval=false \
           : var=RETURN # sval=false

Each button definition has two parts separated by =:

Label — the text shown on the button (label=DEPLOY)
One or more posts — separated by :, each post being a var/sval (string) or var/dval (double/numeric) pair

So clicking DEPLOY above posts three variables simultaneously to the MOOSDB:

DEPLOY = "true"
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE = "false"
RETURN = "false"

A companion button might be:

BUTTON_TWO = label=RETURN # var=RETURN # sval=true \
           : var=DEPLOY # sval=false
The # delimiter

Within a single post clause, # separates the fields:

var=DEPLOY # sval=true

This is not a comment — it's pMarineViewer's field separator. Many people trip over this because # is a comment character in most other MOOS config contexts.

Common mistakes that make a button appear but do nothing

1. Wrong variable name (case mismatch)

MOOS variable names are case-sensitive. If your pHelmIvP block subscribes to DEPLOY but your button posts Deploy or deploy, the helm never sees it. The button renders fine, the post fires, but nothing changes.

2. Posting a string when a numeric value is expected (or vice versa)

Use sval for string values and dval for doubles. If a behavior conditions on DEPLOY == 1.0 (numeric) but you post sval=true, the condition evaluates to false and the behavior never activates.

3. Missing or wrong condition in the behavior

The button posts correctly, but the behavior in pHelmIvP has a condition = DEPLOY=true line that never evaluates to true because some other required condition (e.g. RETURN=false) isn't set. All conditions on a behavior must be satisfied simultaneously.

4. MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE left as true

If MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=true is in the MOOSDB (e.g. from a previous state or as a default), pHelmIvP suppresses all output regardless of what DEPLOY says. A correct deploy button must post MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false at the same time as DEPLOY=true.

5. Syntax error in the button definition silently drops posts

A malformed clause (e.g. vvar=DEPLOY or missing # between fields) often causes pMarineViewer to render the button but silently ignore that clause. Always check the terminal output of pMarineViewer at startup — it will warn about malformed button parameters.

6. Not subscribing / helm not running

If pHelmIvP hasn't started yet or crashed, the variable gets posted to the MOOSDB but nobody reads it. The button looks fine, mission stays inert.

Quick mental model
Button click
    └─► pMarineViewer posts var=VAL to MOOSDB
            └─► pHelmIvP reads MOOSDB, checks conditions
                    └─► if ALL conditions true → behavior activates → actuator commands

Any break in that chain — wrong name, wrong type, unsatisfied co-condition, helm suppressed — and the button fires into the void.

gemini.text:
In pMarineViewer, action buttons are defined inside its configuration block in your shoreside .moos file. When clicked, these buttons execute "pokes" (publications) to the MOOSDB to alter the vehicle's state or behavior modes.

Here is exactly how they are configured and the common slip-ups that render them useless.

1. How Action Buttons Are Configured

Buttons are defined using the BUTTON parameter. The general syntax requires a label followed by one or more variable-value pairs separated by #.

The key variables you mentioned—DEPLOY, MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE, and RETURN—are usually bundled into buttons like this:

Code snippet
ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer
{
  // ... other parameters ...

  // Button 1: Puts the helm into DRIVE state and activates the deploy behavior
  BUTTON = DEPLOY # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false # DEPLOY=true # RETURN=false

  // Button 2: Safely halts the mission, putting the vehicle in manual override (PARK)
  BUTTON = HALT   # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=true

  // Button 3: Tells the helm to abort current tasks and return home
  BUTTON = RETURN # RETURN=true # DEPLOY=false
}

Key Formatting Rules:

The first item after BUTTON = is always the text that appears physically on the button GUI (e.g., DEPLOY, HALT, RETURN).

The # character acts as a delimiter to separate the button name from the commands, as well as to chain multiple variable postings together.

The $ symbol can be used for macros, such as logging a timestamp via $[UTC], if needed.

2. Common Mistakes: Why a Button Appears But Fails to Work

It is a common rite of passage in MOOS-IvP to click a beautifully rendered button only for your vehicle to sit completely still. If the button is visible in the GUI but does nothing, check for these five common mistakes:

1. Typo in MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE (The Legacy "R")

Historically, MOOS used a misspelled variable: MOOS_MANUAL_OVERIDE (with one 'R'). While modern versions of pHelmIvP accept both the correct and incorrect spellings, legacy missions, third-party apps, or specific configurations might only listen to one. If your button sets MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false but the vehicle remains in PARK, check your helm logs to see which spelling your specific helm build is subscribing to.

2. Missing String Quotes in the Configuration

MOOS is highly literal about data types. If a variable is expected as a string, omitting or misusing quotes can cause pHelmIvP to ignore it.

Correct: DEPLOY=true (The helm reads this as a string matching its logic conditions).

Wrong: DEPLOY="true" (If the behavior condition is just looking for DEPLOY=true, the literal inclusion of double quotes in the MOOS DB might break the string match).

3. The Shore-to-Vehicle "pShare" Disconnect

In a multi-vehicle or simulated setup, pMarineViewer runs on the shoreside community, but the helm (pHelmIvP) runs on the vehicle community.

When you click the button, pMarineViewer pokes the shoreside MOOSDB.

If your pShare configuration is missing or broken, that variable never crosses the bridge to the vehicle's MOOSDB. The button looks like it works on your screen, but the vehicle is completely deaf to it.

4. Behavior Condition Mismatch

A button only posts data; it doesn't force a behavior to run. For DEPLOY=true or RETURN=true to actually do something, a behavior in your .bhv file must be actively listening for it.
If your button says:

Code snippet
BUTTON = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true

But your Loiter behavior in the .bhv file says:

Code snippet
condition = DEPLOYMT=true   <-- Typo in the behavior file!

The variable is updated perfectly in the database, but the behavior stays idle.

5. Competing "Logic Contradictions"

If your DEPLOY button sets DEPLOY=true but fails to explicitly clear the return flag (i.e., it leaves RETURN=true in the database from a previous click), a logic contradiction occurs. In the .bhv file, if the Return behavior has a higher priority than the Deploy behavior, the vehicle will stubbornly remain in Return mode despite your frantic clicking of the Deploy button. Always ensure your buttons explicitly "turn off" opposing states.

Flash

chatgpt_55_instant.text:
In pMarineViewer, action buttons are configured inside its ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer block in the .moos file.

Typical pattern:

moos
ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer
{
  button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true
  button_one = MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false # RETURN=false
  button_two = RETURN # RETURN=true
}

This means:

Click DEPLOY:
  post DEPLOY=true
  post MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false
  post RETURN=false

Click RETURN:
  post RETURN=true

The label before # is the button text. The part after # is the MOOS poke. Multiple lines with the same button number add multiple posts to the same button. MOOS-IvP docs describe this as mission-specific configuration, not hard-coded behavior; the Alpha mission uses exactly this pattern. 
OceanAI

Common mistakes:

moos
button_one = DEPLOY=true

This may make the label wrong or fail to define the intended poke. Use:

moos
button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true

Other failure modes:

The button is in the wrong config block, so pMarineViewer never reads it.

The variable name is misspelled, for example MOOS_MANUAL_OVERIDE.

The value type/string does not match the behavior condition, for example behavior expects RETURN = true but button posts RETURN=TRUE, return=true, or another variable.

The button posts to the shoreside MOOSDB, but the vehicle helm needs the variable in the vehicle community. In that case, configure pShare/uField messaging correctly or put the button in the right community.

The helm is still parked because you posted only DEPLOY=true but forgot:

moos
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false

The .bhv file conditions do not actually use the variable you are posting.

Best verification: click the button, then use uXMS, uQueryDB, pMarineViewer scope, or the .alog to confirm that DEPLOY, MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE, and RETURN were posted in the MOOSDB where pHelmIvP is running.
